column5: fear of missed opportunities as time runs out
column6: Mit Mitte dreißig begann sie, eine leichte Torschlusspanik zu verspüren.
column7: In her mid-thirties she began to feel a slight fear of missed opportunities.
column8: Literally 'panic of the closing gates', from medieval city gates that shut at dusk: whoever was left outside spent the night in darkness and danger.

column5: to make worse while trying to improve
column6: Er hat den Text verschlimmbessert, jetzt klingt er noch schlechter.
column7: He made the text worse while trying to improve it — now it sounds even worse.
column8: A blend of 'verschlimmern' (to worsen) and 'verbessern' (to improve): a masterful example of German compressing an ironic observation into one word.

column6: Ihr Sprachgefühl macht sie zur herausragenden Autorin.
column7: Her feel for language makes her an outstanding author.
column8: A 19th-century loan into English linguistics: it describes a native speaker's intuitive mastery that no grammar fully captures.

column6: Seine Weltfremdheit macht ihn liebenswert und zugleich handlungsunfähig.
column7: His unworldliness makes him endearing and, at the same time, unable to act.
column8: Tied to the Romantic idealization of the artist-genius: spiritually elevated but practically inept, a figure celebrated by Hölderlin and Novalis.

column5: perseverance / ability to sit something through
column6: Für diese Doktorarbeit braucht man wirklich Sitzfleisch.
column7: This dissertation really requires the ability to sit and stick with it.
column8: Literally 'sitting flesh': adopted into English academic and diplomatic circles for the virtue of patient, dogged effort.

column5: the predicament of having to explain oneself
column6: Nach dem Skandal befand sich der Minister in echter Erklärungsnot.
column7: After the scandal, the minister was in real trouble explaining himself.
column8: The compound with 'Not' (need, distress) gives an emotional weight English lacks: in German political debate, 'in Erklärungsnot' signals an almost total collapse of credibility.

column6: Beim Zuschauen empfand sie tiefes Fremdschämen.
column7: Watching, she felt deep vicarious embarrassment.
column8: Research has confirmed it as a distinct neurological response: mirror neurons fire empathetic embarrassment even for strangers' mistakes.

column6: Die Zweckentfremdung von Wohnraum ist in Berlin verboten.
column7: Repurposing housing away from its intended use is banned in Berlin.
column8: Berlin's 'Zweckentfremdungsverbot' bans turning apartments into tourist rentals — a legal concept so charged it fuels a Europe-wide debate over Airbnb and the right to housing.

column6: Schlimmstenfalls müssen wir das Projekt abbrechen.
column7: In the worst case, we'll have to abandon the project.
column8: It pairs with its opposite 'bestenfalls' (best case): a duo reflecting the German rhetorical tradition of mapping every possibility before deciding.

column6: Diese Klausel ist die Sollbruchstelle des ganzen Vertrags.
column7: This clause is the whole contract's predetermined breaking point.
column8: An engineering term (the point where a part is designed to give way to protect the rest) borrowed into political language for an agreement's deliberate weak spot.

column6: Der Aufsatz war so verquast, dass niemand die These verstand.
column7: The essay was so muddled that no one understood the thesis.
column8: A learned, scornful adjective reserved for thought hiding behind convoluted prose — a frequent weapon of German literary criticism.

column6: Die Entscheidung war weniger Idealismus als nüchterne Realpolitik.
column7: The decision was less idealism than sober power politics.
column8: Coined in 1853 by Ludwig von Rochau and linked to Bismarck: it entered dozens of languages to denote politics driven by power relations, not principles.

column6: In dem Bericht habe es geheißen, alle Beteiligten seien informiert gewesen.
column7: The report reportedly said all parties had been informed.
column8: The past Konjunktiv I ('habe geheißen', 'seien gewesen') carries whole paragraphs of reported speech in German journalism without ever repeating 'according to the report'.

column5: a complex, tangled situation of competing interests
column6: In dieser politischen Gemengelage ist kein einfacher Kompromiss möglich.
column7: In this tangled political situation, no simple compromise is possible.
column8: Originally a land-registry term for scattered, intermixed plots of land: borrowed into politics for situations where too many interests overlap.

column6: Die Kosten sind ins Aberwitzige gestiegen.
column7: Costs have risen to absurd levels.
column8: 'Aber-' here is an old intensifier (as in 'Aberglaube', superstition): not 'but-wit', but 'madness in its purest form'.

column5: to overreach / to bite off more than one can chew
column6: Mit diesem Vorhaben hat sich die Firma verhoben.
column7: With this venture, the company overreached itself.
column8: Literally 'to hurt oneself lifting too heavy a weight': a physical metaphor for miscalibrated ambition, sharper than 'scheitern' (to fail).

column5: the power to define how something is interpreted
column6: Beide Parteien kämpfen um die Deutungshoheit über die Ereignisse.
column7: Both parties are fighting over interpretive dominance over the events.
column8: A compound of 'Deutung' (interpretation) and 'Hoheit' (sovereignty): a key concept in German media debate over who imposes the dominant narrative.

column6: Die Begründung des Gerichts war schlicht hanebüchen.
column7: The court's reasoning was simply outrageous.
column8: From 'Hagebuche' (hornbeam), a knotty, rough wood: originally 'coarse', then 'so crude as to be outrageous'.

column6: Im Nachhinein war der Fehler offensichtlich.
column7: In retrospect, the mistake was obvious.
column8: It pairs with 'im Vorhinein' (in advance): German cleanly lexicalizes the difference between foreseeing and reconstructing.

column5: the height from which one can fall (dramatic stakes)
column6: Je höher der Ruf, desto größer die Fallhöhe.
column7: The higher the reputation, the greater the height from which to fall.
column8: A concept from dramatic theory (Lessing, Schiller): tragedy hits hardest when the character starts from very high up.

column5: to mock / to make fun of
column6: Er fühlte sich von der Presse verhohnepipelt.
column7: He felt mocked by the press.
column8: A colloquial verb, deliberately funny-sounding in form: the clunky sound is itself part of the mockery.

column6: Es fehlt ihm die Muße, ein ganzes Buch zu lesen.
column7: He lacks the unhurried leisure to read a whole book.
column8: Not just any free time but the classics' fruitful otium: 'mit Muße' means doing something calmly, with full attention.

column6: Das ist beileibe keine Kleinigkeit.
column7: That is by no means a small matter.
column8: A fossilized old oath 'bei dem Leibe' ('by [my] body'): it survives almost only before a negation, reinforcing it.

column6: Viele empfinden die neue Vorschrift als reine Gängelei.
column7: Many experience the new rule as sheer over-regulation.
column8: From 'Gängelband', the leading-strings used to hold a child learning to walk: a recurring accusation against a state seen as too intrusive.

column6: Nach der Trennung hatte sie etwas Kummerspeck angesetzt.
column7: After the breakup she had put on some grief weight.
column8: Literally 'grief bacon': the pounds gained by eating to console oneself over emotional pain.

column5: a face that invites a slap
column6: Manche Politiker haben einfach ein Backpfeifengesicht.
column7: Some politicians simply have a punchable face.
column8: A jokey, fairly informal compound: 'Backpfeife' (slap) + 'Gesicht' (face) — popular but best used cautiously.

column5: the perfect retort thought of too late
column6: Mir fiel die perfekte Antwort erst als Treppenwitz ein.
column7: The perfect answer only occurred to me as a staircase wit.
column8: Literally 'staircase joke': the clever reply you only think of after leaving the conversation.

column5: vivid mental imagery / imagination running wild
column6: Bei diesem Buch läuft sofort das Kopfkino.
column7: With this book the mental movie starts running immediately.
column8: Literally 'head cinema': a text's capacity to generate vivid mental images, often anxious ones too.

column6: Im Winter packt mich immer das Fernweh.
column7: In winter, wanderlust always grips me.
column8: The exact opposite of Heimweh: literally 'pain for distance', the aching desire for far-off places.

column6: Er blickte weltschmerzlich aus dem Fenster.
column7: He looked out the window world-wearily.
column8: An adjective derived from 'Weltschmerz', used in a literary register to describe a look steeped in disillusionment.

column5: earworm (catchy tune stuck in your head)
column6: Dieser Song ist ein echter Ohrwurm.
column7: This song is a real earworm.
column8: Literally 'ear worm': a melody that repeats obsessively in the mind — a term that has passed into English too.

column6: Er hat den Job nur dank Vitamin B bekommen.
column7: He only got the job thanks to Vitamin B.
column8: A pun on 'Vitamin B' and 'Beziehungen' (connections): having the right contacts opens doors.

column6: Er will immer eine Extrawurst.
column7: He always wants special treatment.
column8: Literally 'extra sausage': demanding an exception or preferential treatment compared to everyone else.

column5: someone who looks tall while seated but isn't
column6: Er ist ein typischer Sitzriese.
column7: He's a typical 'sitting giant'.
column8: A jokey term for someone with a long torso who looks tall seated at a table but is average or short standing up.

column6: Die Kinder schlagen Purzelbäume im Garten.
column7: The children are doing somersaults in the garden.
column8: 'Einen Purzelbaum schlagen' is the fixed expression for 'to do a somersault', a playful term typical of children's language.

column6: Das war eine echte Schnapsidee.
column7: That was a real harebrained idea.
column8: Literally 'schnapps idea': a plan so absurd it seems to have been conceived under the influence of alcohol.

column6: Er gilt als naiver Weltverbesserer.
column7: He's seen as a naive do-gooder.
column8: Literally 'world improver': often used with mild irony for someone naively idealistic but well-meaning.

column6: Sei kein Korinthenkacker!
column7: Don't be such a nitpicker!
column8: An informal, mildly vulgar term for someone obsessively focused on tiny details, often in an irritating way.

column6: Ich empfand richtige Fremdscham bei dieser Rede.
column7: I felt genuine vicarious embarrassment during that speech.
column8: 'Empfinden' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to feel (an emotion)', more formal than 'fühlen'.

column6: Nach der Trennung hatte er großen Herzschmerz.
column7: After the breakup he had great heartache.
column8: 'Herzschmerz' combines 'Herz' (heart) and 'Schmerz' (pain): the classic romantic ache, often used with affection.

column6: Ich vertraue meinem Bauchgefühl.
column7: I trust my gut feeling.
column8: Literally 'belly feeling': instinctive intuition set against rational reasoning.

column6: Beim Volksfest gibt es Fingerhakeln.
column7: At the folk festival there's finger wrestling.
column8: An old Bavarian strength sport in which two contenders hook fingers and try to pull each other across a table.

column6: Sei kein Weichei, trau dich!
column7: Don't be a wimp, go for it!
column8: Literally 'soft egg': a colloquial, slightly jokey term for someone seen as too timid or fearful.

column5: someone considered soft or overly cautious
column6: In den Bergen nennt man ihn spöttisch Warmduscher.
column7: In the mountains they mockingly call him a 'warm-showerer'.
column8: Literally 'warm shower taker': an ironic term for someone seen as too comfort-loving or unadventurous.

column6: In der Küche herrschte ein echtes Kuddelmuddel.
column7: The kitchen was in a real muddle.
column8: A colloquial, onomatopoeic term for a disorderly mess, of Low German origin, used affectionately.

column6: Der Weg verläuft im Zickzack den Berg hinauf.
column7: The path zigzags up the mountain.
column8: 'Im Zickzack' is a fixed adverbial expression for describing an irregular, jerky route.

column6: Das Museum zeigt historische Kuriositäten.
column7: The museum shows historical curiosities.
column8: 'Kuriosität' describes an unusual, fascinating object or fact, distinct from 'Neugier', the psychological trait of curiosity.

column6: Kadavergehorsam widerspricht demokratischen Werten.
column7: Blind obedience contradicts democratic values.
column8: Literally 'corpse obedience': absolute obedience devoid of critical thought, historically associated with Prussian militarism.

column6: Ihre Scheinheiligkeit war kaum zu ertragen.
column7: Her hypocrisy was almost unbearable.
column8: 'Scheinheiligkeit' combines 'Schein' (appearance) and 'heilig' (holy): literally 'false holiness', moralistic hypocrisy.

column6: Seine Reue waren nur Krokodilstränen.
column7: His remorse was only crocodile tears.
column8: An idiom identical in German and English, referring to fake, manipulative crying.

column6: Man machte ihn zum Sündenbock.
column7: They made him the scapegoat.
column8: 'Machen zu' takes the dative after 'zu': 'zum Sündenbock' — a fixed structure for a role transformation.

column6: Das Gesetz gilt vielen als trojanisches Pferd.
column7: The law is seen by many as a Trojan horse.
column8: 'Gelten als' takes the nominative after 'als', used to describe a measure that conceals a different intent.

column6: Die Logistik ist die Achillesferse des Unternehmens.
column7: Logistics is the company's Achilles' heel.
column8: A classic mythological reference, used in German exactly as in English for a decisive weak point.

column6: Die Kündigung hing wie ein Damoklesschwert über ihm.
column7: The dismissal hung over him like a sword of Damocles.
column8: 'Hängen wie' describes a constant, looming danger — a classical image identical across many European languages.

column6: Der Wahlsieg entpuppte sich als Pyrrhussieg.
column7: The election win turned out to be a Pyrrhic victory.
column8: 'Sich entpuppen als' takes the nominative after 'als', used to reveal something's true nature behind appearances.

column6: Die Reise wurde zu einer echten Odyssee.
column7: The trip turned into a real odyssey.
column8: A Homeric reference used figuratively for a long, difficult experience full of unforeseen twists.

column6: Die Renovierung glich einer Sisyphusarbeit.
column7: The renovation resembled a Sisyphean task.
column8: A reference to the Greek myth of Sisyphus, used for a never-ending, seemingly pointless job.

column6: Die Reform öffnete eine Büchse der Pandora.
column7: The reform opened a Pandora's box.
column8: 'Die Büchse der Pandora öffnen' is the standard fixed expression, referring to the Greek myth of an evil unleashed irreversibly.

column6: Man durchschlug den gordischen Knoten radikal.
column7: They cut the Gordian knot radically.
column8: 'Den gordischen Knoten durchschlagen' means solving a seemingly unsolvable problem with a drastic solution.

column6: Nach dem Umzug wollte sie Tabula rasa machen.
column7: After the move, she wanted to make a clean break.
column8: 'Tabula rasa machen' is a Latin expression fully integrated into German for a fresh start.

column6: Das Ende wirkt wie ein Deus ex Machina.
column7: The ending feels like a deus ex machina.
column8: A classical Latin theatrical term, used in literary criticism for a sudden, implausible narrative solution.

column6: Die Situation gleicht einem Vexierbild.
column7: The situation resembles a puzzle picture.
column8: 'Vexierbild' describes an image that looks different depending on how it's viewed, used figuratively for ambiguous situations.

column6: Die Erbschaft entpuppte sich als Danaergeschenk.
column7: The inheritance turned out to be a poisoned gift.
column8: A reference to the Trojan horse offered by the Danaans (Greeks): a gift concealing negative consequences.

column6: Mit dieser Entscheidung überschritt er den Rubikon.
column7: With this decision he crossed the Rubicon.
column8: A historical reference to Caesar, used for a decisive point of no return.

column6: Dieses Dokument war der Ariadnefaden im Chaos der Akten.
column7: This document was the Ariadne's thread in the chaos of the files.
column8: A reference to the Minotaur myth, used for a clue or tool that lets one navigate a complex situation.

column6: Man sollte dem Sirenengesang des schnellen Geldes widerstehen.
column7: One should resist the siren song of easy money.
column8: 'Widerstehen' takes the dative: 'dem Sirenengesang', used for a dangerous, seductive attraction.

column6: Seine Karriere endete wie ein Ikarusflug.
column7: His career ended like an Icarus flight.
column8: A mythological reference to Icarus, used for excessive ambition leading to a ruinous fall.

column6: Die Norm wirkt wie ein Prokrustesbett für individuelle Fälle.
column7: The norm acts like a Procrustean bed for individual cases.
column8: A mythological reference to Procrustes, used for a rigid rule that artificially forces every case into one standard.

column6: Sein Blick blieb unergründlich.
column7: His gaze remained unfathomable.
column8: 'Unergründlich' combines 'un-' and 'ergründen' (to get to the bottom of something): literally 'without a reachable bottom'.

column6: Die Motive des Täters bleiben unauslotbar.
column7: The perpetrator's motives remain unfathomable.
column8: 'Unauslotbar' comes from 'ausloten' (to sound/plumb), a nautical term applied metaphorically to psychological depth.

column6: Das Gespräch verlief völlig unergiebig.
column7: The conversation turned out to be completely unproductive.
column8: 'Unergiebig' comes from 'ergiebig' (fruitful, productive), a formal adjective used for disappointing results.

column6: Diese Maßnahme wirkt kontraproduktiv.
column7: This measure seems counterproductive.
column8: 'Kontraproduktiv' is a Latin-German loan, used to describe an action with the opposite of its intended effect.

column6: Das System wirkt zunehmend selbstreferenziell.
column7: The system seems increasingly self-referential.
column8: 'Selbstreferenziell' combines 'selbst' and 'referenziell' (referring to), used in philosophy, logic, and media criticism.

column6: Diese Definition ist rein tautologisch.
column7: This definition is purely tautological.
column8: 'Tautologisch' comes from the Greek 'tauto' (same) and 'logos' (word): a definition that repeats itself without adding information.

column6: Er äußerte sich apodiktisch zu diesem Thema.
column7: He spoke apodictically on this topic.
column8: 'Apodiktisch' comes from Greek, a Kantian philosophical term for a statement presented as absolutely certain, beyond doubt.

column6: Seine Pläne wirkten zunehmend chimärisch.
column7: His plans seemed increasingly chimerical.
column8: 'Chimärisch' comes from the mythological monster Chimera: a fascinating but unrealizable idea, pure fantasy.

column6: Diese Hoffnung erwies sich als illusorisch.
column7: This hope turned out to be illusory.
column8: 'Sich erweisen als' takes the nominative after 'als', a fixed structure for revealing something's true nature.

column6: Nehmen wir hypothetisch an, das stimmt.
column7: Let's hypothetically assume that's true.
column8: 'Annehmen' always takes the accusative or a 'dass' clause, used to introduce a hypothetical scenario.

column6: Kontrafaktische Geschichtsschreibung ist umstritten.
column7: Counterfactual historiography is controversial.
column8: 'Kontrafaktisch' describes 'what if' scenarios alternative to real history, a debated historiographical genre.

column6: Diese Prämisse wird axiomatisch vorausgesetzt.
column7: This premise is presupposed axiomatically.
column8: 'Vorausgesetzt werden' is passive, used in mathematics and logic for a principle accepted without proof.

column6: Man kann das nicht a priori ausschließen.
column7: One cannot rule that out a priori.
column8: A Latin expression fully integrated into German philosophical language, denoting knowledge independent of experience.

column6: Diese Erkenntnis gewinnt man nur a posteriori.
column7: This insight is gained only a posteriori.
column8: The opposite of 'a priori': knowledge acquired only through experience, after the fact.

column6: Sein Schreibstil ist sehr idiosynkratisch.
column7: His writing style is very idiosyncratic.
column8: 'Idiosynkratisch' comes from the Greek 'idios' (one's own) and 'synkrasis' (mixture): distinctively personal and peculiar.

column6: Sein Geschmack ist wunderbar eklektisch.
column7: His taste is wonderfully eclectic.
column8: 'Eklektisch' comes from the Greek 'eklegein' (to select): something combining diverse elements drawn from varied sources.

column6: Der Roman wirkt leider epigonal.
column7: The novel unfortunately comes across as epigonal.
column8: 'Epigonal' comes from 'Epigone' (a lesser imitator): a work that unoriginally copies an earlier model.

column6: Ihre Begeisterung war genuin.
column7: Her enthusiasm was genuine.
column8: 'Genuin' is a high-register Latin loanword, a formal synonym for 'echt' (authentic, real).

column6: Diese vermeintlich unbestreitbare These wird nun infrage gestellt.
column7: This supposedly indisputable thesis is now being questioned.
column8: 'Infrage gestellt werden' is passive, used to describe an established belief being called into question.

column6: Die Entscheidungsprozesse bleiben opak.
column7: The decision-making processes remain opaque.
column8: 'Opak' literally describes something not transparent to light, used figuratively for unclear processes.

column6: Das Milieu wirkt nach außen hermetisch abgeschlossen.
column7: The milieu appears hermetically sealed off from outside.
column8: 'Hermetisch' comes from the god Hermes Trismegistus, associated with secret alchemical texts: something completely sealed.

column6: Die beiden Weltanschauungen sind inkommensurabel.
column7: The two worldviews are incommensurable.
column8: A philosophical term from Thomas Kuhn for two scientific paradigms that cannot be measured against the same yardstick.

column5: a change that makes things worse while trying to improve
column6: Die neue Regel ist eine reine Verschlimmbesserung.
column7: The new rule is a pure worsening disguised as improvement.
column8: A noun derived from the verb 'verschlimmbessern', with the same ironic blend of worsening and improving.

column6: Sein Erklärungsversuch überzeugte niemanden.
column7: His attempt at explanation convinced no one.
column8: 'Erklärungsversuch' combines 'Erklärung' (explanation) and 'Versuch' (attempt): an explicit admission of uncertainty about the outcome.

column6: Das war nur eine billige Ausflucht.
column7: That was just a cheap evasion.
column8: 'Ausflucht' comes from 'ausfliehen' (to flee out): an excuse used to escape a responsibility.

column6: Diese Beschönigung täuscht niemanden.
column7: This glossing-over fools no one.
column8: 'Beschönigung' comes from 'beschönigen' (to gloss over): the linguistic attempt to make something appear better than it is.

column6: Das ist doch reine Wortklauberei.
column7: But that's pure word-splitting.
column8: 'Wortklauberei' combines 'Wort' (word) and 'klauben' (to pick minutely): an excess of linguistic pedantry.

column6: Hör auf mit der Haarspalterei!
column7: Stop splitting hairs!
column8: Literally 'splitting hairs': excessive pedantic precision in a discussion, often irritating.

column6: Diese Formulierung ist sprachlicher Krampf.
column7: This phrasing is a linguistic contortion.
column8: 'Krampf' literally means 'cramp': used figuratively for something unnatural and forced, often stylistically.

column6: Hinter dem Sprachgeklingel steckt wenig Substanz.
column7: Behind the empty flowery language there's little substance.
column8: 'Sprachgeklingel' combines 'Sprache' and 'Geklingel' (jingling): elegant language empty of real content.

column6: Politische Reden bestehen oft aus Worthülsen.
column7: Political speeches often consist of empty phrases.
column8: 'Worthülse' combines 'Wort' (word) and 'Hülse' (shell, husk): a word emptied of real meaning through overuse.

column6: Die Rede war reine Phrasendrescherei.
column7: The speech was pure clichéd waffle.
column8: 'Phrasendrescherei' combines 'Phrase' (cliché) and 'dreschen' (to thresh): mechanically churning out platitudes.

column6: Das war doch nur Wischiwaschi.
column7: That was just wishy-washy nonsense.
column8: A colloquial, onomatopoeic term for vague talk with no solid content, very informal.

column6: Seine Selbstgerechtigkeit ging vielen auf die Nerven.
column7: His self-righteousness got on many people's nerves.
column8: 'Selbstgerechtigkeit' combines 'selbst' and 'Gerechtigkeit' (justice): the moralistic conviction of always being right.

column6: Seine ständige Rechthaberei nervt.
column7: His constant need to be right is annoying.
column8: 'Rechthaberei' comes from 'recht haben' (to be right): the compulsive need to always be right in exchanges.

column6: Seine Besserwisserei macht ihn unbeliebt.
column7: His know-it-all behaviour makes him unpopular.
column8: 'Besserwisserei' comes from 'Besserwisser' (know-it-all, one who always knows better): an often-irritating character trait.

column6: Lass endlich die Klugscheißerei!
column7: Quit being a smart-ass already!
column8: A vulgar but extremely common term in informal speech, for someone who arrogantly, pedantically corrects others.

column6: In der Buchhaltung ist Erbsenzählerei manchmal nötig.
column7: In bookkeeping, pea-counting is sometimes necessary.
column8: 'Erbsenzählerei' combines 'Erbsen' (peas) and 'zählen' (to count): an obsession with tiny, irrelevant details.

column6: Soziale Medien fördern die Selbstdarstellung.
column7: Social media encourage self-promotion.
column8: 'Selbstdarstellung' combines 'selbst' and 'Darstellung' (presentation): the curated way one shows oneself to others.

column6: Der Film verzichtet erfreulicherweise auf Effekthascherei.
column7: The film happily forgoes cheap sensationalism.
column8: 'Effekthascherei' combines 'Effekt' (effect) and 'haschen' (to grab greedily): chasing superficial effects to impress.

column6: Kritiker sprechen von reiner Schaufensterpolitik.
column7: Critics speak of pure window-dressing politics.
column8: 'Schaufensterpolitik' combines 'Schaufenster' (shop window) and 'Politik': showy but substantively empty political measures.

column6: Das war nur eine Alibihandlung.
column7: That was just a token gesture.
column8: 'Alibihandlung' combines 'Alibi' and 'Handlung' (action): an action taken only to appear to have done something.

column5: fig leaf (excuse to cover something up)
column6: Die Spende ist nur ein Feigenblatt.
column7: The donation is just a fig leaf.
column8: 'Feigenblatt' alludes to the biblical leaf used to cover nakedness: a superficial cover for something problematic.

column6: Die Präsentation wirkte wie ein Potemkinsches Dorf.
column7: The presentation felt like a Potemkin village.
column8: A historical reference to the fake facades allegedly built by the Russian general Potemkin to impress Catherine II.

column6: Die nostalgische Verklärung der Vergangenheit ist gefährlich.
column7: The nostalgic idealisation of the past is dangerous.
column8: 'Verklärung' comes from 'verklären' (to transfigure): the process of remembering something as better than it really was.

column6: Mit leiser Wehmut dachte sie an früher.
column7: With quiet wistfulness she thought of the old days.
column8: 'Wehmut' combines 'Weh' (pain) and 'Mut' (archaically: state of mind): a sweet, not desperate, sadness.

column6: Die Sehnsucht nach dem Meer wurde immer stärker.
column7: The longing for the sea grew ever stronger.
column8: 'Sehnsucht' combines 'sehnen' (to yearn) and 'Sucht' (addiction): an almost obsessive desire for something distant.

column6: Die Vergänglichkeit des Lebens berührte ihn tief.
column7: The transience of life touched him deeply.
column8: 'Vergänglichkeit' comes from 'vergänglich' (transient, fleeting), a central theme in German Baroque poetry (Vanitas).

column6: Die Endlichkeit des Lebens gibt ihm Sinn.
column7: The finitude of life gives it meaning for him.
column8: 'Endlichkeit' is an existentialist philosophical concept, referring to human awareness of one's own mortality.

column6: Eine sanfte Melancholie durchzog den Film.
column7: A gentle melancholy ran through the film.
column8: 'Durchziehen' isn't separable and takes a direct accusative object, meaning 'to pervade, run entirely through'.

column6: Eine tiefe Schwermut lag über der Stadt.
column7: A deep gloom hung over the city.
column8: 'Schwermut' combines 'schwer' (heavy) and 'Mut' (state of mind): a deeper, darker sadness than 'Wehmut'.

column6: Das Unternehmen verlor seine Daseinsberechtigung.
column7: The company lost its reason for existing.
column8: 'Daseinsberechtigung' combines 'Dasein' (existence) and 'Berechtigung' (right, justification): the very justification for existing.

column6: Seine Weltgewandtheit beeindruckte alle Gäste.
column7: His worldliness impressed all the guests.
column8: 'Weltgewandtheit' combines 'Welt' (world) and 'gewandt' (adept, skilled): a refined ease acquired through travel.

column6: Ihre Lebensklugheit half ihr in jeder Krise.
column7: Her practical wisdom helped her through every crisis.
column8: 'Lebensklugheit' combines 'Leben' (life) and 'Klugheit' (intelligence), distinct from theoretical wisdom: wisdom gained by living.

column6: Altersweisheit lässt sich nicht erzwingen.
column7: The wisdom of old age can't be forced.
column8: 'Sich erzwingen lassen' with a negation means 'cannot be forced': a reflexive-passive structure.

column6: Manche nennen die Jüngeren die Weltschmerzgeneration.
column7: Some call the younger generation the world-weary generation.
column8: A journalistic neologism combining 'Weltschmerz' and 'Generation', describing widespread pessimism among today's young people.

column6: Zukunftsangst prägt viele junge Menschen.
column7: Fear of the future shapes many young people.
column8: 'Prägen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to shape, deeply characterize', used for a widespread condition.

column6: In manchen Debatten herrscht eine regelrechte Untergangsstimmung.
column7: In some debates a veritable sense of doom prevails.
column8: 'Untergangsstimmung' combines 'Untergang' (decline, ruin) and 'Stimmung' (mood): a collective existential pessimism.

column6: Ein kleiner Hoffnungsschimmer blieb ihnen.
column7: A small glimmer of hope remained for them.
column8: 'Hoffnungsschimmer' combines 'Hoffnung' (hope) and 'Schimmer' (glimmer, gleam): a faint but present hope.

column6: Trotz allem bewahrte sie ihre Zuversicht.
column7: Despite everything, she kept her confident optimism.
column8: 'Zuversicht' is deeper and more stable than mere 'Hoffnung': a confidence rooted in the future despite adversity.

column5: zest for life / will to live
column6: Nach der Krankheit fand er neuen Lebensmut.
column7: After the illness he found new zest for life.
column8: 'Lebensmut' combines 'Leben' (life) and 'Mut' (courage): the courage and enthusiasm needed to face life.

column6: Politikverdrossenheit ist eine Form der Weltverdrossenheit.
column7: Political disaffection is a form of world-weariness.
column8: 'Weltverdrossenheit' combines 'Welt' (world) and 'verdrossen' (discontented, disillusioned), a high-register term.

column6: Politikverdrossenheit spiegelt sich in sinkender Wahlbeteiligung.
column7: Political disaffection is reflected in falling voter turnout.
column8: 'Sich spiegeln in' takes the dative: 'in sinkender Wahlbeteiligung', a fixed structure for indicating where a phenomenon shows up.

column6: Angesichts der Tragödie herrschte kollektive Sprachlosigkeit.
column7: In the face of the tragedy, collective speechlessness prevailed.
column8: 'Angesichts' takes the genitive and is typical of the formal-narrative register for introducing a shocking event.

column6: Fassungslosigkeit machte sich unter den Zuschauern breit.
column7: Utter bewilderment spread among the spectators.
column8: 'Sich breitmachen' is separable and reflexive, meaning 'to spread, take hold', used for collective emotions.

column6: Das Ohnmachtsgefühl war fast unerträglich.
column7: The feeling of powerlessness was almost unbearable.
column8: 'Ohnmachtsgefühl' combines 'Ohnmacht' (powerlessness, literally 'without power') and 'Gefühl' (feeling).

column5: spirit of new beginnings / optimistic momentum
column6: Nach der Wende herrschte eine große Aufbruchsstimmung.
column7: After the turning point, a great spirit of new beginnings prevailed.
column8: 'Aufbruchsstimmung' combines 'Aufbruch' (departure, new start) and 'Stimmung' (mood): the exact opposite of 'Untergangsstimmung'.

column6: Man warf ihm Erbschleicherei vor.
column7: He was accused of inheritance hunting.
column8: 'Erbschleicherei' combines 'Erbe' (inheritance) and 'schleichen' (to sneak/creep in): manipulating someone to obtain an inheritance.

column6: Vetternwirtschaft untergräbt das Vertrauen in Institutionen.
column7: Nepotism undermines trust in institutions.
column8: 'Vetternwirtschaft' combines 'Vetter' (cousin) and 'Wirtschaft' (economy/management): favoring relatives and friends in public appointments.

column6: Das Postengeschacher nach der Wahl empört viele Bürger.
column7: The horse-trading over positions after the election outrages many citizens.
column8: 'Postengeschacher' combines 'Posten' (post, office) and 'schachern' (to haggle): opaque dealing over public offices.

column6: Der lokale Klüngel kontrolliert die Vergabe.
column7: The local cronyism clique controls the allocations.
column8: 'Klüngel' describes an informal group trading favors at the expense of transparency, a very Rhineland term.

column6: Der politische Filz behindert echte Reformen.
column7: Entrenched political cronyism hinders real reforms.
column8: 'Filz' literally means 'felt': the image of intertwined, opaque ties between politics and business.

column6: Das Bauprojekt gilt als Vorzeigeprojekt der Stadt.
column7: The construction project is considered the city's flagship project.
column8: 'Vorzeigeprojekt' combines 'vorzeigen' (to proudly show off) and 'Projekt': a project used to make a good public impression.

column6: Das teure Museum wurde als Prestigeobjekt kritisiert.
column7: The expensive museum was criticized as a prestige project.
column8: 'Als kritisiert werden' is passive with 'als', used to criticize a project motivated more by image than utility.

column6: Die Spende dient offensichtlich der Imagepflege.
column7: The donation obviously serves image cultivation.
column8: 'Dienen' takes the dative: 'der Imagepflege', a fixed structure for indicating an action's instrumental purpose.

column6: Umweltschützer werfen der Firma Greenwashing vor.
column7: Environmentalists accuse the company of greenwashing.
column8: 'Vorwerfen' takes the dative of the accused person/entity and the accusative of the accusation: 'der Firma Greenwashing vorwerfen'.

column6: Das Bio-Siegel entpuppte sich als Etikettenschwindel.
column7: The organic seal turned out to be label fraud.
column8: 'Etikettenschwindel' combines 'Etikette' (label) and 'Schwindel' (deception): when what's stated doesn't match reality.

column6: Diese Reform ist reine Augenwischerei.
column7: This reform is pure eyewash.
column8: Literally 'wiping the eyes': an action taken only to create an illusion of progress, with no real substance.

column6: Der neue Vertrag ist eine echte Mogelpackung.
column7: The new contract is a real deceptive package.
column8: 'Mogelpackung' combines 'mogeln' (to cheat) and 'Packung' (package): a product that promises more than it actually contains.

column6: Der glamouröse Auftritt war reines Blendwerk.
column7: The glamorous appearance was pure dazzling deception.
column8: 'Blendwerk' combines 'blenden' (to dazzle) and 'Werk' (work): something created to dazzle and hide a lack of substance.

column6: Das ganze Verfahren war nur Mummenschanz.
column7: The whole procedure was just a masquerade.
column8: An archaic term tied to medieval carnival games, used today figuratively for an elaborate charade.

column6: Die Verhandlung entpuppte sich als reine Scharade.
column7: The negotiation turned out to be a pure charade.
column8: 'Scharade' is a loan from French, used figuratively for a staged performance lacking authenticity.

column6: Der Prozess wurde zu einer Farce.
column7: The trial turned into a farce.
column8: 'Zu etwas werden' expresses a transformation: 'wurde zu einer Farce', a critical judgment on a process that degenerated.

column6: Seine Worte trieften vor Hohn.
column7: His words dripped with scorn.
column8: 'Triefen vor' takes the dative: 'vor Hohn', a vivid expression describing speech full of mockery.

column6: Die Kritik war voller Häme.
column7: The criticism was full of spiteful gloating.
column8: 'Häme' is nearly a synonym of 'Schadenfreude' but more aggressive, with a note of deliberate cruelty.

column6: Reine Bosheit steckte hinter dieser Bemerkung.
column7: Pure malice was behind that remark.
column8: 'Bosheit' comes from 'böse' (evil) with the abstract suffix '-heit', a high-register term for intentional malice.

column6: Solche Niedertracht hatte niemand erwartet.
column7: No one had expected such vileness.
column8: 'Niedertracht' combines 'nieder' (low) and 'Tracht' (bearing, demeanor): morally contemptible behavior.

column6: Die Verlogenheit der Aussage war offensichtlich.
column7: The mendacity of the statement was obvious.
column8: 'Verlogenheit' comes from 'verlogen' (mendacious, lying), a high-register term for deep, habitual dishonesty.

column6: Man wirft der Regierung Doppelmoral vor.
column7: The government is accused of double standards.
column8: 'Vorwerfen' takes the dative of the accused entity and the accusative of the accusation, as with 'Greenwashing vorwerfen'.

column6: Die Position enthält einen inneren Selbstwiderspruch.
column7: The position contains an inner self-contradiction.
column8: 'Enthalten' is not separable and always takes a direct accusative object, used to identify an internal logical flaw.

column6: Als Künstler ist er ein echter Grenzgänger zwischen den Stilen.
column7: As an artist he is a true boundary-crosser between styles.
column8: 'Grenzgänger' literally means 'one who crosses the border', but is often used figuratively for someone working between different fields.

column6: Migranten leben oft in einer Zwischenwelt.
column7: Migrants often live in an in-between world.
column8: 'Zwischenwelt' combines 'zwischen' (between) and 'Welt' (world): an existential space neither fully in one place nor the other.

column6: Er sprach von einer inneren Heimatlosigkeit.
column7: He spoke of an inner homelessness.
column8: 'Heimatlosigkeit' comes from 'heimatlos' (homeless, without a homeland), used existentially rather than literally, as a lack of belonging.

column6: Wurzellosigkeit prägt viele Einwandererfamilien.
column7: Rootlessness characterizes many immigrant families.
column8: 'Wurzellosigkeit' comes from 'wurzellos' (rootless): the lack of a stable bond to a place or tradition.

column6: Bikulturalität bringt Reichtum und Spannungen zugleich.
column7: Biculturalism brings both richness and tensions at once.
column8: 'Zugleich' means 'at the same time', used to indicate two coexisting, often contradictory, qualities or effects.

column6: Die Expedition war eine echte Grenzerfahrung.
column7: The expedition was a true boundary experience.
column8: 'Grenzerfahrung' combines 'Grenze' (border, limit) and 'Erfahrung' (experience): an experience that pushes to human limits.

column6: Sie befand sich in einem inneren Ausnahmezustand.
column7: She was in a state of inner emergency.
column8: 'Ausnahmezustand' literally means '(legal) state of emergency', used here metaphorically for extreme inner turmoil.

column6: Die Grenzüberschreitung wurde als Kunst gefeiert.
column7: The transgression was celebrated as art.
column8: 'Gefeiert werden als' is passive with 'als', used to describe a controversial act presented positively.

column6: Der Tabubruch löste heftige Reaktionen aus.
column7: The taboo-breaking triggered fierce reactions.
column8: 'Auslösen' is separable and takes the accusative, meaning 'to trigger, set off', used for intense social reactions.

column6: Das Kunstwerk war als Provokation gedacht.
column7: The artwork was intended as a provocation.
column8: 'Gedacht sein als' means 'to be conceived as', a fixed structure for describing the intent behind an action.

column6: Subversion durch Kunst hat eine lange Tradition.
column7: Subversion through art has a long tradition.
column8: 'Durch' always takes the accusative, used to indicate the means through which an action or influence occurs.

column6: Sein künstlerisches Grenzgängertum machte ihn berühmt.
column7: His artistic boundary-crossing existence made him famous.
column8: The suffix '-tum' forms neuter abstract nouns referring to a lasting condition or state, as in 'Rittertum' (knighthood).

column6: Kritiker warnen vor der kommerziellen Vereinnahmung.
column7: Critics warn against commercial co-optation.
column8: 'Warnen vor' takes the dative: 'vor der Vereinnahmung', a fixed structure for a warning about a risk.

column6: Kulturelle Aneignung wird kontrovers diskutiert.
column7: Cultural appropriation is discussed controversially.
column8: 'Kontrovers diskutiert werden' is passive, a standard structure for describing a hotly debated public topic.

column6: Der Selbstermächtigungsdiskurs prägt viele soziale Bewegungen.
column7: The discourse of self-empowerment shapes many social movements.
column8: A very long compound typical of academic public-discourse analysis, combining 'Selbstermächtigung' and 'Diskurs'.

column6: Es besteht eine deutliche Repräsentationslücke.
column7: There is a clear representation gap.
column8: 'Bestehen' is often used without a preposition and is irregular: 'besteht, bestand, bestanden', used for an existing fact.

column6: Sichtbarmachung ist ein erster Schritt zur Gleichstellung.
column7: Making visible is a first step toward equality.
column8: 'Sichtbarmachung' combines 'sichtbar' (visible) and 'machen' (to make): the process of giving public visibility to a group or issue.

column6: Historische Unsichtbarmachung betrifft viele Randgruppen.
column7: Historical erasure affects many marginalized groups.
column8: The exact opposite of 'Sichtbarmachung': the historical process of ignoring or erasing certain groups from the dominant narrative.

column6: Randgruppen finden selten Gehör in der Politik.
column7: Marginalized groups rarely find a hearing in politics.
column8: 'Gehör finden' is the fixed collocation for 'to find a hearing, to be heard', often used in political and social contexts.

column6: Die Mehrheitsgesellschaft muss sich öffnen.
column7: The majority society must open itself up.
column8: 'Mehrheitsgesellschaft' combines 'Mehrheit' (majority) and 'Gesellschaft' (society), a key term in integration discourse.

column6: Jedes System hat einen Sollbruchpunkt.
column7: Every system has a predetermined breaking point.
column8: A variant of 'Sollbruchstelle', used figuratively for the moment when a system or relationship is bound to give way.

column6: Die Verhandlung wurde als Nullsummenspiel wahrgenommen.
column7: The negotiation was perceived as a zero-sum game.
column8: 'Wahrgenommen werden als' is passive with 'als', a game-theory term applied to political negotiations.

column6: Beide Seiten profitieren von dieser Win-win-Situation.
column7: Both sides benefit from this win-win situation.
column8: A full English loanword, widely integrated into German negotiating and business language.

column6: Die Themen dienen nur als Verhandlungsmasse.
column7: The issues only serve as bargaining chips.
column8: 'Dienen als' takes the nominative after 'als', used to indicate that something functions as an instrumental means in a negotiation.

column6: Die Verhandlungen enden in einer Pattsituation.
column7: The negotiations end in a stalemate.
column8: 'Patt' comes from the French 'pat' (checkmate by stalemate), used figuratively for any unresolved impasse.

column6: Die Diskussion ist in einer Sackgasse angekommen.
column7: The discussion has arrived at a dead end.
column8: 'Sackgasse' literally means 'street with no exit', often used figuratively for a situation with no possible progress.

column6: Armut und schlechte Bildung bilden einen Teufelskreis.
column7: Poverty and poor education form a vicious circle.
column8: 'Teufelskreis' combines 'Teufel' (devil) and 'Kreis' (circle): a self-perpetuating negative cycle that's hard to escape.

column6: Erfolg erzeugt oft eine Aufwärtsspirale.
column7: Success often creates an upward spiral.
column8: The opposite of 'Teufelskreis': a positive cycle that reinforces itself over time.

column6: Die Firma steckte in einer Abwärtsspirale.
column7: The company was stuck in a downward spiral.
column8: 'Stecken in' takes the dative: 'in einer Abwärtsspirale', a fixed structure for describing a situation that's hard to escape.

column6: Ein Bankrott löste einen Domino-Effekt aus.
column7: A bankruptcy triggered a domino effect.
column8: 'Auslösen' is separable and takes the accusative, used for a series of consecutive events caused by a single initial event.

column6: Der Fehler entwickelte sich zum Schneeballeffekt.
column7: The mistake developed into a snowball effect.
column8: 'Sich entwickeln zu' takes the dative after 'zu', a fixed structure for a progressive transformation into something bigger.

column6: Das Urteil gilt als Dammbruch für ähnliche Fälle.
column7: The ruling is considered a breach of the dam for similar cases.
column8: 'Dammbruch' literally means 'breach of a dam', used figuratively for a decision that opens the floodgates for many others.

column6: Diese Entscheidung hat eine große Präzedenzwirkung.
column7: This decision has a major precedent effect.
column8: 'Präzedenzwirkung' combines the Latin loan 'Präzedenz' and 'Wirkung' (effect), a formal legal-political term.

column6: Die Maßnahme hatte einen unerwarteten Bumerangeffekt.
column7: The measure had an unexpected boomerang effect.
column8: 'Bumerangeffekt' describes when an action comes back against whoever took it, with consequences contrary to those intended.

column6: Die Kürzungen verursachten erheblichen Kollateralschaden.
column7: The cuts caused considerable collateral damage.
column8: 'Verursachen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to cause', a formal, non-separable verb.

column6: Die Reform hatte unerwünschte Nebenwirkungen.
column7: The reform had undesired side effects.
column8: 'Unerwünscht' combines the negating 'un-' and 'erwünscht' (desired): a side effect explicitly not wanted.

column6: Das ist kein Einzelfall, sondern ein Systemfehler.
column7: This is not an isolated case, but a systemic flaw.
column8: 'Kein ..., sondern' is a fixed contrastive structure for denying one explanation and proposing a deeper alternative.

column6: Ein struktureller Mangel liegt der Krise zugrunde.
column7: A structural deficiency underlies the crisis.
column8: 'Zugrunde liegen' takes the dative: 'der Krise', a formal fixed structure for indicating the deep cause of a problem.

column6: Das ist ein blinder Fleck in ihrer Argumentation.
column7: That is a blind spot in her argument.
column8: 'Blinder Fleck' comes from eye anatomy, used figuratively for an aspect systematically ignored in a line of reasoning.

column6: Diese Denkfalle tappen viele Menschen.
column7: Many people fall into this thought trap.
column8: 'In eine Falle tappen' is the fixed expression for 'to fall into a trap', here used for a common cognitive error.

column6: In der Sitzung herrschte eine babylonische Sprachverwirrung.
column7: In the meeting a Babylonian confusion of tongues prevailed.
column8: A biblical reference to the Tower of Babel, used figuratively for total miscommunication among participants.

column6: Die Debatte verkam zur reinen Kakophonie der Meinungen.
column7: The debate degenerated into a pure cacophony of opinions.
column8: 'Verkommen zu' takes the dative after 'zu', a fixed structure for describing degradation into something negative.

column6: Ein lautes Stimmengewirr erfüllte den Saal.
column7: A loud confused babble of voices filled the hall.
column8: 'Stimmengewirr' combines 'Stimmen' (voices) and 'Gewirr' (tangle, confusion): the sound of many overlapping voices.

column6: Die Vertragsklauseln sind reines Kauderwelsch.
column7: The contract clauses are pure gibberish.
column8: A pejorative term for confusing, technical, or foreign language completely incomprehensible to the listener.

column6: Bitte erklären Sie das ohne Fachchinesisch.
column7: Please explain that without technical jargon.
column8: Literally 'technical Chinese': a colloquial expression for specialist jargon impossible for laypeople to understand.

column6: Die Präsentation strotzte vor Buzzwords.
column7: The presentation was bursting with buzzwords.
column8: 'Strotzen vor' takes the dative: 'vor Buzzwords', used critically for an excess of trendy but empty terms.

column6: Die Anglizismenflut in der Werbung nervt viele.
column7: The flood of anglicisms in advertising annoys many people.
column8: 'Anglizismenflut' combines 'Anglizismen' and 'Flut' (flood): a critical image of the excessive use of English loanwords.

column6: Manche Verwaltungsbegriffe klingen wie Neusprech.
column7: Some administrative terms sound like newspeak.
column8: A calque of Orwell's 'Newspeak' from '1984', used for manipulative or euphemistic institutional language.

column6: Die Neusprachlichkeit der Werbebranche ist auffällig.
column7: The neologistic tendency of the advertising industry is striking.
column8: 'Auffällig' means 'noticeable, conspicuous', used to describe a striking linguistic feature.

column6: 'Rindfleischetikettierungsüberwachungsaufgabenübertragungsgesetz' war ein berühmtes Wortungetüm.
column7: 'Rindfleischetikettierungsüberwachungsaufgabenübertragungsgesetz' was a famous monstrous word.
column8: 'Wortungetüm' jokingly describes excessively long German compounds, often from law or administration.

column6: Der Autor liebt lange Bandwurmsätze.
column7: The author loves long tapeworm sentences.
column8: Literally 'tapeworm sentence': a sentence so long and intricate it seems as endless as a parasitic worm.

column6: Kant schreibt oft in komplizierten Schachtelsätzen.
column7: Kant often writes in complicated nested sentences.
column8: 'Schachtelsatz' combines 'Schachtel' (box) and 'Satz' (sentence): sentences with clauses nested one inside another.

column6: Die Verschachtelung der Sätze erschwert das Verständnis.
column7: The nesting of the sentences makes understanding difficult.
column8: 'Erschweren' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to make difficult', a formal, non-separable verb.

column6: Der Nominalstil macht Behördentexte oft unverständlich.
column7: The nominal style often makes bureaucratic texts incomprehensible.
column8: 'Nominalstil' describes a style that replaces verbs with abstract nouns, typical of and criticized in bureaucratic German.

column6: Übermäßige Passivkonstruktionen wirken distanziert.
column7: Excessive passive constructions come across as distant.
column8: 'Wirken' means 'to appear, to give the impression of', used to describe the stylistic effect of a grammatical choice.

column6: Behördendeutsch schreckt viele Bürger ab.
column7: Officialese scares many citizens off.
column8: 'Abschrecken' is separable and takes the accusative, meaning 'to deter, intimidate', used for off-putting language.

column6: Die Verklausulierung des Vertrags macht ihn undurchsichtig.
column7: The excessive clausing of the contract makes it opaque.
column8: 'Verklausulierung' comes from 'Klausel' (clause): the excess of fine print and sub-clauses that makes a text opaque.

column6: Die Website ist eine reine Textwüste.
column7: The website is a pure wall of text.
column8: 'Textwüste' combines 'Text' and 'Wüste' (desert): a written page devoid of visual structure, hard to read.

column6: Der Kanzler sprach von einer Zeitenwende.
column7: The chancellor spoke of a turning point of an era.
column8: 'Zeitenwende' became famous in 2022 as a political term describing a radical shift in German security policy.

column6: Die fortgesetzte Vergangenheitsbewältigung prägt die deutsche Politik.
column7: The ongoing reckoning with the past shapes German politics.
column8: 'Fortgesetzt' comes from 'fortsetzen' (to continue): it stresses that the process of historical reckoning is never finished.

column6: Das Nie-wieder-Gelöbnis prägt jede Gedenkfeier.
column7: The never-again pledge shapes every commemoration ceremony.
column8: 'Nie-wieder-Gelöbnis' combines the phrase 'nie wieder' (never again) and 'Gelöbnis' (solemn vow), central to German memory culture.

column6: Die 'Stunde Null' von 1945 wird historisch diskutiert.
column7: The 'zero hour' of 1945 is discussed historically.
column8: A controversial historical term describing 1945 as an absolute new beginning, an idea now critically reassessed by historians.

column6: Das Wirtschaftswunder veränderte Westdeutschland grundlegend.
column7: The economic miracle fundamentally changed West Germany.
column8: A historical term for West Germany's rapid economic reconstruction in the 1950s, after the devastation of the war.

column6: Die Nachkriegsgeneration hatte andere Werte.
column7: The post-war generation had different values.
column8: 'Nachkriegsgeneration' combines 'Nachkrieg' (post-war) and 'Generation', a key term in German social-historical studies.

column6: Man beschimpfte ihn als Wendehals.
column7: He was insulted as a turncoat.
column8: An ironic, derogatory term for someone who quickly switched political convictions after the Wall fell in 1990.

column6: Ostalgie zeigt sich in DDR-Produkten im Supermarkt.
column7: Nostalgia for East Germany shows up in GDR products in the supermarket.
column8: A blend of 'Ost' (east) and 'Nostalgie' (nostalgia), a complex cultural phenomenon tied to the memory of East Germany.

column5: the wall in the mind (lingering East-West divide)
column6: Die Mauer im Kopf existiert manchmal noch immer.
column7: The wall in the mind still sometimes exists.
column8: A fixed expression describing the persistent cultural and mental differences between former East and West Germany, over thirty years later.

column6: Der Aufarbeitungsprozess ist noch nicht abgeschlossen.
column7: The process of reckoning is not yet finished.
column8: 'Abgeschlossen' comes from 'abschließen' (to conclude), often used to say a historical process is still ongoing.

column6: Kritiker sprechen von reiner Symbolpolitik.
column7: Critics speak of pure symbolic politics.
column8: 'Symbolpolitik' combines 'Symbol' and 'Politik': showy political measures without substantial practical effect.

column6: Das Konzentrationslager ist heute ein Erinnerungsort.
column7: The concentration camp is today a site of memory.
column8: A historiographical concept (Pierre Nora's 'lieu de mémoire'), referring to places that embody a nation's collective memory.

column6: Manche kritisieren eine oberflächliche Betroffenheitskultur.
column7: Some criticize a superficial culture of performative concern.
column8: A critical term for a public expression of moral concern perceived as superficial or ritualistic.

column6: Erinnerungspolitik prägt das nationale Selbstverständnis.
column7: The politics of memory shapes national self-understanding.
column8: 'Prägen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to shape, deeply characterize'.

column6: Geschichtsbewusstsein wird schon in der Schule vermittelt.
column7: Historical consciousness is already conveyed in school.
column8: 'Vermitteln' takes an (optional) dative and an accusative, a formal verb used in educational contexts.

column6: Der Autor beeindruckt durch seine Sprachgewalt.
column7: The author impresses through his linguistic power.
column8: 'Sprachgewalt' combines 'Sprache' (language) and 'Gewalt' (power, force): an almost overwhelming mastery of language.

column6: Ihre Wortgewaltigkeit fesselte das Publikum.
column7: Her verbal forcefulness captivated the audience.
column8: 'Fesseln' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to chain, to captivate', a verb used for magnetic speech.

column6: Die Sprachmächtigkeit dieses Dichters ist beeindruckend.
column7: This poet's command of language is impressive.
column8: Nearly a synonym of 'Sprachgewalt', but with a slightly more formal, literary nuance.

column6: Das Sonett zeigt eine erstaunliche Formvollendung.
column7: The sonnet shows an astonishing perfection of form.
column8: 'Formvollendung' combines 'Form' (form) and 'Vollendung' (perfect completion), a term from literary and artistic criticism.

column6: Seine Diktion ist präzise und klar.
column7: His diction is precise and clear.
column8: 'Diktion' describes an author's overall style of expression, not just pronunciation as in Italian.

column6: Der Sprachduktus verrät den Autor sofort.
column7: The stylistic tone gives away the author immediately.
column8: 'Duktus' comes from the Latin 'ducere' (to lead): the distinctive, recognizable trait of someone's writing style.

column6: Seine Wortgewandtheit half ihm in jeder Debatte.
column7: His verbal eloquence helped him in every debate.
column8: 'Wortgewandtheit' combines 'Wort' and 'gewandt' (adept): the ability to always find the right words at the right moment.

column6: Ihre Redegewandtheit überzeugte selbst Skeptiker.
column7: Her eloquence in speech convinced even skeptics.
column8: 'Selbst' as an adverb means 'even', used to intensify a statement with an extreme case.

column6: Seine Beredsamkeit war schon in der Antike legendär.
column7: His eloquence was legendary already in antiquity.
column8: 'Beredsamkeit' is a more archaic, literary variant of 'Redegewandtheit', used mainly in historical or classical contexts.

column6: Seine natürliche Eloquenz war unverkennbar.
column7: His natural eloquence was unmistakable.
column8: 'Eloquenz' is a direct loan from Latin, nearly identical to English, used in a high register.

column6: Ein feines Sprachgefühl zeichnet gute Übersetzer aus.
column7: A fine sense of language distinguishes good translators.
column8: 'Auszeichnen' is separable and takes the accusative, meaning 'to distinguish', used for a distinctive quality.

column6: Das Gedicht besticht durch seine Ausdruckskraft.
column7: The poem impresses through its expressive power.
column8: 'Bestechen durch' takes the accusative after 'durch', a fixed structure for praising an extraordinary quality.

column6: Die sprachliche Sinnlichkeit dieses Textes ist selten.
column7: The linguistic sensuousness of this text is rare.
column8: 'Sinnlichkeit' comes from 'Sinn' (sense), referring to a text's ability to evoke vivid sensory experiences.

column6: Die Bildhaftigkeit seiner Sprache fasziniert.
column7: The vividness of his language fascinates.
column8: 'Bildhaftigkeit' comes from 'bildhaft' (figurative, evocative), referring to a text's ability to create mental images.

column6: Der Dichter betreibt regelrechte Wortmalerei.
column7: The poet engages in veritable word painting.
column8: 'Wortmalerei' combines 'Wort' (word) and 'Malerei' (painting): language used so vividly it 'paints' mental images.

column6: Er hatte Gewissensbisse wegen der Lüge.
column7: He had pangs of conscience because of the lie.
column8: 'Gewissensbisse' combines 'Gewissen' (conscience) and 'Bisse' (bites): literally 'bites of conscience', always plural.

column6: Sie steckte in einem echten Gewissenskonflikt.
column7: She was caught in a real conflict of conscience.
column8: 'Stecken in' takes the dative: 'in einem Konflikt', a fixed structure for describing being in a difficult situation.

column6: Ein tiefes Schuldgefühl plagte ihn seit Jahren.
column7: A deep feeling of guilt had plagued him for years.
column8: 'Plagen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to torment, afflict', a formal, non-separable verb.

column6: Am Ende der Geschichte steht seine Läuterung.
column7: At the end of the story stands his moral redemption.
column8: 'Läuterung' comes from 'läutern' (to purify), a literary term for a character's moral transformation.

column6: Die Tragödie bewirkt eine echte Katharsis beim Publikum.
column7: The tragedy brings about a genuine catharsis in the audience.
column8: An Aristotelian concept from the 'Poetics', adopted wholesale into German to describe emotional purification through art.

column6: Der Läuterungsprozess dauerte Jahre.
column7: The process of purification took years.
column8: 'Läuterungsprozess' combines 'Läuterung' and 'Prozess', used for a long personal path toward redemption.

column6: Er suchte nach Sühne für seine Taten.
column7: He sought atonement for his deeds.
column8: 'Suchen nach' takes the dative: 'nach Sühne', a fixed structure for expressing the search for something abstract.

column6: Vergeltung löst selten echte Gerechtigkeit aus.
column7: Retribution rarely produces true justice.
column8: 'Auslösen' is separable and takes the accusative, meaning 'to produce, trigger', often used critically.

column6: Er bat um Gnade.
column7: He begged for mercy.
column8: 'Bitten um' takes the accusative: 'um Gnade', a fixed structure for a formal request, often in a legal or religious context.

column6: Vergebung fällt manchmal schwerer als Vergessen.
column7: Forgiveness is sometimes harder than forgetting.
column8: 'Schwerer fallen als' takes the dative and a comparative, a fixed structure for expressing that something is harder than something else.

column6: Echte Reue zeigte er nie.
column7: He never showed genuine remorse.
column8: 'Zeigen' takes a direct accusative object, no preposition, a common verb for displaying an emotion or quality.

column6: Seine Bußfertigkeit wirkte aufrichtig.
column7: His contrition seemed sincere.
column8: 'Bußfertigkeit' combines 'Buße' (penance) and 'fertig' (ready): the inner readiness to atone for a wrongdoing.

column6: Wiedergutmachung kann nie alles heilen.
column7: Reparation can never heal everything.
column8: 'Wiedergutmachung' combines 'wieder' (again), 'gut' (good) and 'machen' (to make): literally 'to make good again', to right a wrong.

column6: Der Sieg verschaffte ihr große Genugtuung.
column7: The victory brought her great satisfaction.
column8: 'Verschaffen' takes the dative of the person and the accusative of the thing obtained, a formal, non-separable verb.

column6: Ein kurzes Triumphgefühl durchflutete ihn.
column7: A brief feeling of triumph flooded through him.
column8: 'Durchfluten' is not separable and takes a direct accusative object, literally 'to flood completely', used figuratively.

column6: Prophylaxe ist besser als Behandlung.
column7: Prevention is better than treatment.
column8: 'Prophylaxe' comes from the Greek 'prophylassein' (to guard beforehand): the medical prevention of an illness before it manifests.

column6: Salutogenese fragt, was Menschen gesund erhält.
column7: Salutogenesis asks what keeps people healthy.
column8: A concept coined by sociologist Aaron Antonovsky, opposed to 'Pathogenese', which studies the causes of illness.

column6: Soziale Unterstützung ist ein wichtiger Resilienzfaktor.
column7: Social support is an important resilience factor.
column8: 'Resilienzfaktor' combines 'Resilienz' and 'Faktor', a key term in contemporary positive psychology.

column6: Ärzte sollten stärker salutogenetisch denken.
column7: Doctors should think more salutogenically.
column8: 'Stärker' intensifies the verb, indicating a greater degree of applying a mental approach.

column6: Ein starkes Kohärenzgefühl schützt vor Stress.
column7: A strong sense of coherence protects against stress.
column8: A central Antonovsky concept: the perception that one's life is comprehensible, manageable, and meaningful.

column6: Verletzlichkeit zu zeigen erfordert Mut.
column7: Showing vulnerability requires courage.
column8: 'Zu zeigen' as a 'zu'-infinitive functions as the subject of the sentence, a common construction in formal German.

column6: Ambiguitätstoleranz hilft beim interkulturellen Lernen.
column7: Tolerance of ambiguity helps with intercultural learning.
column8: 'Ambiguitätstoleranz' is a key psychological term for the ability to handle uncertain or contradictory situations.

column6: Interkulturelle Kompetenz wird im Beruf immer wichtiger.
column7: Intercultural competence is becoming ever more important in the workplace.
column8: 'Immer wichtiger' strengthens the comparative with 'immer', indicating a progressively growing importance.

column6: Diese Situation erfordert viel Feingefühl.
column7: This situation requires a lot of tact.
column8: 'Feingefühl' combines 'fein' (fine, refined) and 'Gefühl' (feeling): a perceptive delicacy in human relations.

column6: Sie hat einen guten Spürsinn für Talente.
column7: She has a good nose for talent.
column8: 'Spürsinn' combines 'spüren' (to sense, perceive) and 'Sinn' (sense): an almost infallible instinct for recognizing something.

column6: Er hat ein besonderes Gespür für Trends.
column7: He has a special feel for trends.
column8: 'Gespür für' takes the accusative: 'für Trends', a fixed structure for expressing a specific intuition in a field.

column6: Diese Entscheidung zeugt von großem Weitblick.
column7: This decision testifies to great foresight.
column8: 'Zeugen von' takes the dative: 'von Weitblick', a fixed structure meaning 'to testify to, denote' a quality.

column6: Politische Weitsicht ist selten geworden.
column7: Political far-sightedness has become rare.
column8: Nearly a synonym of 'Weitblick', often used in long-term political and strategic contexts.

column6: Sein analytischer Scharfsinn beeindruckte alle.
column7: His analytical acumen impressed everyone.
column8: 'Scharfsinn' combines 'scharf' (sharp) and 'Sinn' (sense): a sharp, penetrating intelligence.

column6: Die alte Weisheitslehre bleibt aktuell.
column7: The ancient wisdom teaching remains relevant.
column8: 'Weisheitslehre' combines 'Weisheit' (wisdom) and 'Lehre' (teaching), referring to ancient philosophical or spiritual traditions.

column6: In der Krise verlor er jegliches Fingerspitzengefühl.
column7: In the crisis he lost all sense of tact.
column8: 'Jeglich' means 'any, every', an indefinite pronoun of higher register, more formal than 'jeder'.

column6: Verantwortungsdiffusion erklärt, warum niemand eingreift.
column7: Diffusion of responsibility explains why no one intervenes.
column8: A psychological concept describing how individual responsibility diminishes in the presence of a group, the so-called 'bystander effect'.

column6: Der Zuschauereffekt wurde in vielen Studien bestätigt.
column7: The bystander effect has been confirmed in many studies.
column8: 'Bestätigt werden' is passive, common in research language for describing confirmed experimental results.

column6: Aschs Konformitätsexperiment ist ein Klassiker der Psychologie.
column7: Asch's conformity experiment is a classic of psychology.
column8: A reference to Solomon Asch's famous 1950s experiment on social pressure toward conformity.

column6: Autoritätshörigkeit war zentral für Milgrams Experiment.
column7: Subservience to authority was central to Milgram's experiment.
column8: A reference to Stanley Milgram's famous experiment on blind obedience to authority figures, a much-discussed study.

column6: Gehorsamsbereitschaft variiert stark je nach Kultur.
column7: Readiness to obey varies greatly depending on culture.
column8: 'Je nach' takes the dative: 'je nach Kultur', a fixed structure meaning 'depending on'.

column6: Selbstjustiz ist in einem Rechtsstaat verboten.
column7: Vigilante justice is forbidden in a state governed by the rule of law.
column8: 'Selbstjustiz' combines 'selbst' and 'Justiz' (justice): the illegal act of taking justice into one's own hands, bypassing institutions.

column6: Eine Bürgerwehr patrouilliert nachts durch den Ort.
column7: A citizens' militia patrols the town at night.
column8: 'Bürgerwehr' combines 'Bürger' (citizen) and 'Wehr' (defense): informal groups of civil self-defense, often controversial.

column6: Denunziation war im totalitären System weit verbreitet.
column7: Denunciation was widespread in the totalitarian system.
column8: 'Weit verbreitet sein' means 'to be widespread', a passive-adjectival structure common in historical discourse.

column6: Die Bespitzelung durch die Stasi traumatisierte viele.
column7: Spying by the Stasi traumatized many.
column8: 'Traumatisieren' takes a direct accusative object, a formal verb used in serious historical and psychological contexts.

column6: Manche warnen vor einem digitalen Überwachungsstaat.
column7: Some warn against a digital surveillance state.
column8: 'Warnen vor' takes the dative: 'vor einem Überwachungsstaat', a fixed structure for a warning about a political risk.

column6: Foucault nutzte das Panoptikum als Metapher für Machtstrukturen.
column7: Foucault used the panopticon as a metaphor for power structures.
column8: An architectural concept (Bentham) taken up philosophically by Michel Foucault to describe pervasive social control.

column6: Foucault beschrieb die moderne Disziplinargesellschaft.
column7: Foucault described the modern disciplinary society.
column8: A central Foucauldian concept, referring to how modern institutions (school, prison, hospital) discipline bodies and minds.

column6: Biopolitik betrifft die Steuerung des Lebens durch den Staat.
column7: Biopolitics concerns the state's control over life.
column8: Another Foucauldian concept, referring to how state power manages and regulates the biological life of populations.

column6: Jede Erinnerung hat ihr eigenes Verklärungsmomentum.
column7: Every memory has its own moment of idealisation.
column8: A neologism combining 'Verklärung' and 'Momentum', used in critical analyses of memory and nostalgia.

column6: Die Vergegenwärtigung der Geschichte gelingt dem Museum gut.
column7: The museum succeeds well at making history present.
column8: 'Vergegenwärtigung' comes from 'sich etwas vergegenwärtigen' (to mentally bring something present): making the past vivid.

column6: Zeitgenossenschaft verbindet Menschen unterschiedlichster Herkunft.
column7: Contemporaneity connects people of the most diverse origins.
column8: 'Zeitgenossenschaft' comes from 'Zeitgenosse' (contemporary): the fact of sharing the same historical era.

column6: Kant plädierte für ein Weltbürgertum.
column7: Kant advocated for a cosmopolitan citizenship of the world.
column8: 'Plädieren für' takes the accusative: 'für ein Weltbürgertum', a Kantian philosophical concept of perpetual peace and universal citizenship.

column6: Wir gehören alle zur selben Menschheitsfamilie.
column7: We all belong to the same human family.
column8: 'Gehören zu' takes the dative: 'zur selben Menschheitsfamilie', a fixed structure for expressing collective belonging.

column6: Die Weltgemeinschaft muss gemeinsam handeln.
column7: The world community must act together.
column8: 'Weltgemeinschaft' combines 'Welt' (world) and 'Gemeinschaft' (community), often used in international diplomatic discourse.

column6: Der Klimaschutz ist eine Menschheitsaufgabe.
column7: Climate protection is a task facing all of humanity.
column8: 'Menschheitsaufgabe' combines 'Menschheit' (humanity) and 'Aufgabe' (task): a challenge concerning the entire human species.

column6: Große Nationen tragen eine besondere Weltverantwortung.
column7: Great nations bear a special responsibility toward the world.
column8: 'Tragen' means figuratively 'to bear, take on (a responsibility)', a common use of the verb.

column6: Die Menschenwürde ist unantastbar.
column7: Human dignity is inviolable.
column8: The first article of the German Basic Law: 'Die Würde des Menschen ist unantastbar', one of the constitution's most-cited principles.

column6: Die Unantastbarkeit der Menschenwürde ist unumstößlich.
column7: The inviolability of human dignity is irrefutable.
column8: 'Unumstößlich' means 'unshakeable, incontestable', a very high-register adjective for absolute principles.

column6: Marx beschrieb den Menschen als Gattungswesen.
column7: Marx described the human being as a species-being.
column8: A central concept of the young Marx, referring to the essentially social and creative nature of the human being as a species.

column6: Der Selbstverwirklichungsdrang treibt viele Künstler an.
column7: The drive for self-actualisation motivates many artists.
column8: 'Antreiben' is separable and means 'to drive, motivate', used for a deep inner psychological force.

column6: Ein Kollegenschwein verriet das Projekt an die Konkurrenz.
column7: A backstabbing colleague leaked the project to the competition.
column8: A very informal, mildly vulgar term for a disloyal colleague who betrays coworkers' trust for personal gain.

column6: Kritiker sprechen von einer reinen Ellenbogengesellschaft.
column7: Critics speak of a pure elbow society.
column8: 'Ellenbogengesellschaft' combines 'Ellenbogen' (elbow) and 'Gesellschaft' (society): a society where everyone elbows their way forward.

column6: Unter Kollegen herrscht manchmal Futterneid.
column7: Among colleagues, professional jealousy sometimes prevails.
column8: Literally 'envy over food' (from the animal world): used figuratively for jealousy tied to resources or recognition at work.

column6: Ein leises Futterneidgefühl stieg in ihr auf.
column7: A quiet feeling of professional jealousy rose up in her.
column8: 'Aufsteigen' is separable and uses 'sein' in the perfect tense, describing an emotion that gradually 'rises' in a person.

column6: Futterneid unter Kollegen vergiftet das Betriebsklima.
column7: Professional jealousy among colleagues poisons workplace morale.
column8: 'Vergiften' takes a direct accusative object, meaning 'to poison', used figuratively for a damaged social climate.

column6: Konkurrenzneid ist unter Geschwistern weit verbreitet.
column7: Competitive envy is widespread among siblings.
column8: 'Weit verbreitet sein' means 'to be widespread', a passive-adjectival structure common for general social phenomena.

column6: Geschwisterrivalität ist ein normaler Teil des Aufwachsens.
column7: Sibling rivalry is a normal part of growing up.
column8: 'Geschwisterrivalität' combines 'Geschwister' (siblings) and 'Rivalität' (rivalry), a psychological term from child development.

column6: Berufliche Torschlussangst treibt viele zum Jobwechsel.
column7: Professional deadline anxiety drives many to change jobs.
column8: A variant of 'Torschlusspanik' applied specifically to careers, the fear of professionally 'missing the boat'.

column6: Der Begriff Lebensabschnittspartner klingt bewusst unromantisch.
column7: The term 'life-phase partner' sounds deliberately unromantic.
column8: An ironic, bureaucratic-sounding term coined in the 1980s, used jokingly for a non-permanent partner, almost sardonic.

column6: Verabredungsstress kennt fast jeder Single.
column7: Almost every single person knows dating stress.
column8: 'Verabredungsstress' combines 'Verabredung' (date) and 'Stress', a modern colloquial term tied to dating.

column6: Sein Beziehungsstatus ist kompliziert.
column7: His relationship status is complicated.
column8: 'Beziehungsstatus' combines 'Beziehung' (relationship) and 'Status', a term made famous by social media profiles.

column6: Trennungsschmerz verblasst irgendwann.
column7: Breakup pain fades eventually.
column8: 'Verblassen' means 'to fade, weaken', a poetic verb often used for emotions that lessen over time.

column6: Seine Sturheit brachte das ganze Projekt in Gefahr.
column7: His stubbornness put the whole project at risk.
column8: 'In Gefahr bringen' is a fixed collocation meaning 'to endanger', often used in formal contexts.

column6: Trotz ihrer Dickköpfigkeit respektierten alle sie.
column7: Despite her hardheadedness, everyone respected her.
column8: 'Dickköpfigkeit' combines 'dick' (thick) and 'Kopf' (head): literally 'thick head', a stubborn determination.

column6: Seine Beharrlichkeit zahlte sich am Ende aus.
column7: His persistence paid off in the end.
column8: 'Sich auszahlen' is reflexive and separable, meaning 'to pay off', used for efforts that eventually bear results.

column6: Sie ist ein echter Sturschädel.
column7: She's a real stubborn head.
column8: 'Sturschädel' combines 'stur' (stubborn) and 'Schädel' (skull), a colloquial, affectionate or exasperated term for an obstinate person.

column6: Kinder zeigen früh einen gewissen Eigensinn.
column7: Children show a certain wilfulness early on.
column8: 'Eigensinn' combines 'eigen' (own) and 'Sinn' (sense): the tendency to want to do things one's own way, not necessarily negative.

column6: Die Trotzphase ist für Eltern anstrengend.
column7: The defiant phase is exhausting for parents.
column8: 'Trotzphase' combines 'Trotz' (defiance, spite) and 'Phase': the period of child development marked by tantrums and opposition.

column6: Ihre Bockigkeit nervte die ganze Familie.
column7: Her stubborn sulkiness annoyed the whole family.
column8: 'Bockigkeit' comes from 'bockig' (sulky, stubborn as a billy goat), a colloquial, affectionate or exasperated term.

column6: Seine Unnachgiebigkeit blockierte jede Einigung.
column7: His inflexibility blocked every agreement.
column8: 'Unnachgiebigkeit' combines the negating 'un-' and 'nachgeben' (to yield): an absolute refusal to compromise.

column6: Kompromisslosigkeit kann sowohl Stärke als auch Schwäche sein.
column7: Being uncompromising can be both a strength and a weakness.
column8: 'Sowohl ... als auch' is the fixed structure for 'both ... and', expressing that two qualities coexist in one thing.

column6: Zu viel Nachgiebigkeit wird oft ausgenutzt.
column7: Too much accommodation is often exploited.
column8: 'Ausgenutzt werden' is passive, used to describe how a positive quality can be exploited by others.

column6: Endlich zeigte er Rückgrat.
column7: He finally showed backbone.
column8: 'Rückgrat zeigen' is a fixed idiomatic expression for 'having the courage of one's convictions', literally 'showing the spine'.

column6: Charakterstärke zeigt sich in schwierigen Momenten.
column7: Strength of character shows itself in difficult moments.
column8: 'Sich zeigen in' takes the dative: 'in schwierigen Momenten', a fixed structure for indicating where a quality manifests.

column6: Die Kleinstaaterei prägte Deutschland vor 1871.
column7: Fragmentation into petty states characterized Germany before 1871.
column8: A pejorative historical term for Germany's political fragmentation into hundreds of small states before unification.

column6: Solche Kleinkariertheit hat in einem globalen Markt keinen Platz.
column7: Such narrow-mindedness has no place in a global market.
column8: 'Kleinkariertheit' comes from 'kleinkariert' (small-checkered, i.e., petty): a narrow, pedantic mindset.

column6: Man warf der Debatte Provinzialismus vor.
column7: The debate was accused of provincialism.
column8: 'Vorwerfen' takes the dative of the criticized entity and the accusative of the accusation, as in 'jemandem etwas vorwerfen'.

column6: Fehlende Weltoffenheit bremst die Innovation.
column7: Lacking cosmopolitanism holds back innovation.
column8: 'Bremsen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to brake, hinder', often used in economic and cultural contexts.

column6: Institutionen haben ein enormes Beharrungsvermögen.
